instagram.author: itsthatlady.dev
instagram.body:
If you've been using AI agents for anything complex, you already know this pain.

You have to re-explain everything. Every. Single. Time.

Your agent has no memory between tasks and that's not a small bug. That's a fundamental limitation breaking real workflows right now.

I don't have a solution to his BUT I've been looking into a few things that are aiming to solve this problem.

This is the AI agent conversation nobody's having loudly enough. Until now.
💬 Drop "MEMORY" if you want to look t some resources I've found about managing agent memory.

#aiagents #vibecoding #ai
Your AI agent can think, it can reason, it can solve complex problems, but it cannot remember what it did five minutes ago, and that is a way bigger problem than people realize. Let me explain. So you ask an agent to refactor your code. It does a great job. Then, 20 minutes later, you ask it to add a feature, and it writes code that conflicts with what it just refactored, because it has no memory of the previous task. You have to re-explain everything every single time. And if you've been using AI agents for anything complex, you just nodded your head because you understand. This is the number one unsolved problem in agentic AI right now. There's a post on dev two about it, because every developer is feeling the same way. Agent memory is still an unsolved mystery in the industry right now, but in the meantime, there are a few approaches that you can implement. Comment memory, and I'll send you a list of resources that you can take a look at.
